source_contract.v2: each admitted root-restore macro allocates one fresh extension and then exactly eliminates one live original/root variable
source_contract.v3: runs only after no root variable is live; each admitted tail macro allocates one fresh extension and eliminates two distinct variables live before the macro

definitions.r0: number of variables in the original canonical root CNF
definitions.k2: number of committed v2 macro-restore steps before root-free phase
definitions.h: number of live variables at first root-free v3 entry
definitions.k3: number of committed v3 extension-tail macrosteps
definitions.K: total committed v2+v3 macro extensions k2+k3

lemma_1_root_input_dominates_twice_root_.statement: For every nonterminal nonempty canonical root CNF, N>2r0.
proof: state_units(root)=1+m+L where m is clause count and L is total literal occurrences.
Every root variable occurs in at least one literal, so L>=r0.
A nonempty nonterminal root has m>=1.
Therefore N=state_units(root)+r0=1+m+L+r0>=2+2r0>2r0. The max(2,...) wrapper only strengthens the inequality in degenerate small cases.
Each committed v2 plan chooses its exact elimination pivot from the live original/root variables.
The definitional macro introduces only one fresh extension identifier and no new root identifier.
Exact elimination removes the chosen root pivot, so live-root count decreases by at least one per committed v2 macrostep.
No transition can create a new original/root identifier. Hence at most r0 such v2 commits occur.

lemma_3_root_free_entry_live_count.statement: At first root-free v3 entry, h<=k2.
proof: All original variables are absent by definition of root-free entry.
Before v3 begins, the only transformation in this v2/v3 engine that introduces a new Boolean variable is a committed v2 definitional extension.
Each v2 commit introduces exactly one historical extension identifier.
Pure elimination, unit propagation and exact certificate lanes introduce no variable identifiers.
Therefore every live root-free variable is among the at most k2 extensions introduced earlier, so h<=k2.
v3 requires at least two live variables to commit a plan.
Every committed v3 plan introduces at most one fresh variable and exactly eliminates two distinct variables that were live before the macro.
Hence live-variable count decreases by at least one per v3 commit.
Starting from h live variables, at most h-1 such commits can occur before fewer than two variables remain; earlier terminal or ordinary exact lanes only shorten the suffix.

theorem.name: FROZEN_EXTENSION_CAP_N_DOMINATES_TOTAL_V2_V3_MACRO_COUNT
theorem.statement: For every execution of the frozen v2/v3 engine, K=k2+k3<=2r0-1<N whenever k2>0; if k2=0 then K=0. Therefore the frozen extension_cap=N cannot be exhausted by a sequence of otherwise-admissible v2/v3 macro commits before the macro descent itself is finished.
proof: If k2=0, root-free entry has h=0 under Lemma 3 and no v3 macro is possible or needed, so K=0.
Lemma 1 gives 2r0-1<N.
Since extension_cap=N and extension_count starts at zero and increases by exactly one per committed v2/v3 macro, cap exhaustion cannot precede the maximal structurally possible macro sequence.

consequence_for_open_frontier.note: The theorem does not prove any of these remaining move-availability obligations.
